# Results — Study 620 (A-H Share Premium)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the same
company costs ~30% more in Shanghai than in Hong Kong, and no one can arbitrage it away** —
measured on a fixed panel of **14 dual-listed Chinese companies** (A-share line on the Shanghai
exchange in CNY, H-share line in Hong Kong in HKD; 1:1-par ordinary shares with identical
per-share dividends). Premium = raw A close ÷ (raw H close × HKD→CNY) − 1, the Hang Seng AH
Premium index convention, equal-weight across pairs, monthly. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete month; the sample is sliced there and never creeps). Fingerprint
`f54aaa8986a9`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes, raw + dividend-adjusted: 14 A lines (.SS), 14 H twins (.HK), FX crosses `CNY=X`/`HKD=X` (public, no key) |
| Window | 2010-01-01 → 2026-06-30 (**16.5** years; 4,301 daily rows, **198** complete months) |
| Panel | Ping An, PetroChina, Sinopec, ICBC, Bank of China, CCB, AgBank, China Life, China Merchants Bank, CITIC Securities, China Shenhua, Air China, Tsingtao, Great Wall Motor |
| Premium | per pair, raw `A / (H × HKD→CNY) − 1` (the HSAHP convention); relative-return races use **dividend-adjusted** closes with the H leg converted to CNY (total-return, both legs one currency) |
| Execution / costs | ONE documented lag everywhere: signal = month-end *t* premium, position held month *t+1*; fade costs = one-way bps × 4 legs × membership churn; short legs pay borrow (1.5–3%/yr stress on the H short) |
| Hygiene | Yahoo pre-listing 0.01 placeholders (6030.HK before 2011-10-06) masked; the last month is complete by construction (as-of = month-end) |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The panel is 14 pairs *still dual-listed* in
> 2026 — pairs that delisted or merged away (e.g. Haitong Securities, absorbed in 2025) cannot
> appear, and the panel skews to mega-cap SOEs where the premium is best documented. This tilts
> the *level* toward the well-known wide-premium corner; the cross-sectional and predictive
> tests are within-panel and less exposed.

## The premium level — Shanghai really does pay ~30% more

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **EW mean premium, 2010–2026** | **+29.69%** (the claim says ~30) |
| HAC(12) *t* / HAC(36) *t* on the level | **+5.12** / **+3.29** |
| months positive | **84.8%** of 198 (last negative month: **2014-10**) |
| post-Connect (2014-12 →) | mean **+41.90%**, HAC(12) *t* = **+9.19**, **100%** of 139 months positive |
| as-of level (2026-06-30) | **+33.1%** (range −11.7% → +77.1%) |
| per pair | **13/14** positive means; Great Wall **+83.6%**, China Life **+74.5%** … Ping An **−0.5%** |

**Near-unit-root honesty.** The premium level has AR(1) φ = 0.977 — and our own synthetic
control shows **26/40 zero-mean worlds faking |HAC *t*| ≥ 2** on such a level. So the level
claim also gets a Monte-Carlo placebo (4,000 zero-mean paths with the tape's own persistence
and innovation vol):

| null world | p(mean ≥ +29.7%) | p(share_pos ≥ 84.8%) |
|---|--:|--:|
| calibrated AR(1) (φ = 0.977, innov sd 0.0501) | **0.0177** | 0.0890 |
| stress φ = 0.995 | 0.2372 | 0.2712 |
| driftless random walk from the 2010 start | 0.4405 | 0.5118 |

Under the tape-calibrated null the 16-year average is significant at 5%; under a pure
random-walk null it is **not** — that is the epistemological price of non-convergence, and we
say it out loud. What certifies *structure* is the return-based cross-section below (fade
HAC *t* = +5.09, valid *t* on returns, not levels) plus 139 consecutive positive months since
Stock Connect opened — the very reform that lets the same investor buy both lines.

## Non-convergence — you cannot tell the premium from a random walk

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| AR(1) φ (EW premium, monthly) | **0.977** (se 0.015) → half-life **30.4 months** |
| Dickey-Fuller *t* | **−1.49** vs 5% critical −2.86 → **cannot reject a unit root** |
| per-pair half-lives | median **11.3 months**, range 5.5 – 45.1 |

## Co-movement — one factor, not 14 mispricings

Mean pairwise correlation of monthly premium *changes*: **0.322**; PC1 carries **39.2%** of
the variance (vs 7.1% if independent; 176 complete months). The A-H premium is a single
market-wide segmentation factor that all pairs breathe together.

## The fade trade (PAPER) — the premium *does* predict relative returns

Long H / short A in the widest-premium half of pairs, the reverse in the narrow half; signal =
month-end premium, held the next month (the one documented lag); 0.5× per spread side.

| variant | bps/mo | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **gross, headline** | **+61.9** | **+5.09** (ann +7.68%, churn 11.4%/mo, n = 197) |
| skip-a-month (kills month-end bounce) | +45.5 | +4.84 |
| 2010-01 – 2018-06 | +84.9 | +5.17 |
| 2018-07 – 2026-06 | +36.4 | +2.36 |
| ex 2 extreme pairs (GWM, China Life) | +60.5 | +6.32 |
| **price-only** (no dividends) | +64.1 | +5.38 |
| random halves (**20-seed** baseline) | −2.6 | −0.26 |
| z-portfolio (premium z × next-month H−A) | +63.5 | +5.04 |
| own-history time-series fade | +43.0 | +1.39 |
| unconditional carry (always long H / short A) | +6.8 | +0.26 (price-only +0.6, *t* +0.02) |

The **cross-section** mean-reverts hard (wide pairs' H out-earns their A and vice versa —
*t* ≈ 5 on returns, robust to skip-month, sub-periods, dropping extremes, and price-only), while
the **level** never does (own-history fade *t* = 1.39; carry *t* = 0.26). Pairs revert to the
*pack*, and the pack sits 30–40% above parity.

## Tradability — the alpha lives exactly where you cannot go

The wide half of the fade is **long H / short A** — and *A-shares cannot be shorted* by anyone
who sees this spread: A/H lines are non-fungible, Stock Connect has no securities-lending,
and the domestic relending channel was suspended in 2024. The only executable half is the
narrow-pair **long A (northbound Connect) / short H (HK borrow)**:

| executable half | bps/mo | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| gross | +54.7 | **+2.09** (churn 11.3%/mo) |
| net 25 bps one-way + 1.5%/yr H borrow | +30.9 | **+1.19** (ann +3.77%) |
| net 50 bps one-way + 3.0%/yr H borrow | +7.1 | +0.27 |
| gross 2010-01 – 2018-06 / 2018-07 – 2026-06 | +82.7 / +24.9 | +1.91 / **+0.95** |

Borderline gross, sub-significant net, fading in the recent half — and it is a bet that the
premium *widens*, not an arbitrage of it. **Mirage.**

## Third axis — is the discount side (H) at least the better buy?

Equal-weight total-return baskets, both legs in CNY, 2010-02 → 2026-06 (16.4 years):

| basket | ann. return | wealth |
|---|--:|--:|
| **H (the 30%-cheaper line)** | **+9.36%/yr** | ×4.35 |
| A | +8.13%/yr | ×3.61 |
| H − A | +11.6 bps/mo, HAC *t* = **+0.42** | — |

Sixteen years of buying the same cash flows at a ~30% discount produced **+1.2 pp/yr of
point-estimate and statistically nothing** (*t* = 0.42): the discount never converges, so its
only pay-through is the higher dividend yield — mostly offset by the A line's premium
*widening* over the sample. Both legs quoted gross of dividend withholding (≈10% either
channel for an outside investor; near-symmetric, so it does not flip the race). **Busted.**

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful (never market evidence)

| detector | planted world | null world |
|---|---|---|
| level (40 seeds each) | plant 30% → seed-avg **+29.79%** (sd 4.70) | plant 0% → **−0.21%**; **0/40** seeds reach the real +29.7%; **26/40** fake \|HAC *t*\| ≥ 2 |
| fade (10 seeds each) | φ = 0.97 (mean-reverting premium) → seed-avg *t* **+5.01** | φ = 1.0 (random-walk premium) → *t* **+0.44** |

The level detector recovers a planted premium and no zero-mean world reaches the observed
level — while the HAC-*t*-on-level column is exactly why the real-tape level carries an MC
placebo instead of an HAC certificate. The fade detector fires only when the premium truly
mean-reverts, so the real tape's fade *t* = +5.09 is evidence of genuine cross-sectional
reversion.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The A-H premium averaged **+29.69%** over 16.5 years (HAC(12) *t* = 5.12,
  HAC(36) *t* = 3.29, calibrated-null MC **p = 0.018**), has been positive **139 months in a
  row** since Stock Connect opened, sits in **13/14 pairs**, moves as **one factor** (PC1
  39.2%), and its cross-section predicts relative returns at **HAC *t* = +5.09** on returns —
  robust to skip-month, sub-periods, extremes, price-only, and a 20-seed random baseline.
  Survivorship (still-dual-listed mega-cap panel) named. Stress caveat said out loud: under a
  pure random-walk null the 16-year *average alone* cannot be distinguished from luck
  (p = 0.44) — non-convergence is precisely what makes the level hard to certify, and
  precisely the claim.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The convergence arb does not exist (non-fungible lines, no A-share
  borrow); the profitable half of the fade *requires shorting A*; the only executable half
  (long A / short H) nets *t* = 1.19 at realistic costs and *t* = 0.95 gross since 2018 — and
  is a bet on the premium widening, not an arbitrage. Nothing here survives access + costs.
- **"Is the cheap H line at least the better buy?" — BUSTED.** ×4.35 vs ×3.61 over 16.4 years
  = +11.6 bps/mo at *t* = 0.42: statistically nothing. A 30% discount that never closes pays
  you only its (taxed) dividend edge, and the A line's premium widening ate most of it.
